chunk_findings.detail: When `--landed` is not supplied, the code sets `landing = (None, "")`. A non-empty tuple is truthy, so the later `**({"landed": landing[0]} if landing else {})` and `if landing: dropped = _end_fix_task_landed(log, item, landing[0])` both execute on ordinary bug closures. chunk_findings.detail: The scenario in the bug (B256be593f0) is a fix task that was already CLAIMED when its fix landed elsewhere, so `--landed` must end the caller’s own claimed task. `_landed_elsewhere` deliberately builds an "UNCLAIMED" task and never runs `claim` as the closing agent; the only claimed test (`test_a_task_held_by_someone_else_is_kept`) claims as `--agent other` and asserts the task is kept, not ended. As a result, an implementation that still fails for a self-claimed task—the exact bug being fixed—would leave this suite green while the bug remains.

chunk_findings.detail: `_landing` uses `git merge-base --is-ancestor sha base` to decide whether the landed fix is on the base branch. Git's `--is-ancestor` exits non-zero when the two commits are the same commit: a commit is not considered its own ancestor. Therefore, if the fix has landed as the current tip of `base_ref` (for example, `main` is already at fix commit `C` and the user runs with `--landed C`), `_landing` returns `(None, "... is not on 'main' ...")` and rejects a commit that is plainly on the base. This exactly blocks the “fix already merged as the base tip” case the change is meant to close; use a reachability check that includes equality instead.

chunk_findings.detail: When the user runs `ddflow bug fixed B256be593f0 --landed <commit> --regression-test <test>` with an open fix task, the code verifies the commit and immediately `return _regression_status(status, ev, G)`. This branch never calls the newly added `_end_fix_task_landed`/`_drop_fix_task` helpers, and `_regression_status` receives neither the open `fx` nor `landing` as arguments, so the open fix task is not closed in the task store. The command still prints `bug ... closed`, but the original B256be593f0 condition persists: the fix task remains open and the gates still demand a commit ahead.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `not any(_is_node_id(t) for t in tests)` only refuses `--landed` when no entry is a pytest node id. A `--regression-test` list such as `tests/test_x.py::test_a,tests/test_x.py` yields one node id and one non-node id, so `any` is true and the guard lets the non-node entry through. The guard’s own message says a non-node id “could not be checked”, so this should be `not all(...)` (reject every non-node entry), otherwise a mixed list can bypass the exact unverified-close this check is meant to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_landed_elsewhere`, `tests/<name>` is only written and committed as part of the landing commit (after the pre-fix commit at line 30), so the pre-fix tree `landing^1` does not contain `tests/test_always.py::test_always`. The `ALWAYS_PASSES` test can therefore never actually run before the landing; the pre-fix run will be a missing-test/collection error. The assertion only checks `REFUSED` and `"pre-fix tree"`, so the test would pass even if the implementation incorrectly accepted a test that genuinely passes before the landing. The scenario it claims to cover is not exercised.

chunk_findings.detail: After `landing, why = _landing(...)`, `landing` is already the commit SHA string from `_landing`; `landing[0]` is only its first character. For example, `--landed 1a2b3c4` yields `landing == "1a2b3c4"`, so the `bug.fixed` event records `"landed": "1"`, and `_end_fix_task_landed` is told the landed commit is `"1"` rather than `"1a2b3c4"`. The fix task is then closed against a one-character identifier that does not identify the commit, and downstream readers cannot find the landed fix. Both places should use the full `landing` string, not `landing[0]`.

chunk_findings.detail: When the caller selected a worktree (`tree`) that is not the main repository worktree — for example `ddflow bug fixed B256be593f0 --landed <fix-sha> --tree /repo/wt` — this branch passes the main `repo` object as `verify_regression_test`'s `tree` instead of the enclosing function's `tree` argument. The regression test is then checked out and run in the main repo worktree, ignoring the caller's selected worktree. A test that would fail on `/repo/wt` can be reported as passing (or vice versa), and the main worktree can be left checked out at `landing[0]` as a side effect. It should pass `tree=tree`, like the regression verification path for an existing fix-task landing.

chunk_findings.detail: The test creates the exact B256be593f0 scenario with `_landed_elsewhere`: the current base already contains the landed fix, so `tests/test_f.py::test_f` already passes on the base. It then calls `api.bug_fixed(repo, "B1", regression_test="tests/test_f.py::test_f")` without `landed` and asserts `res.exit == OK`. But the original bug is precisely that this no-landed call refuses because the test passes on the base and there is no first-parent pre-fix tree to prove the test failed. If the implementation makes this assertion true, it now closes a bug without the required pre-fix failure verification; if it preserves the intended refusal, this test fails. Either way the change is wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: The helper always writes the test file in the same commit as the fix, so the landing commit’s first parent does not contain the test file. Thus the pre-fix run of `pytest ... <node id>` is “file or directory not found” (exit code 4), not a real pass or fail. This makes `test_a_test_that_already_passes_before_the_landing_is_refused` invalid: with `ALWAYS_PASSES`, the pre-fix run is absent, not already passing, so an implementation that classifies missing-file as non-zero/failed will return OK and fail the `REFUSED` assertion; if the implementation refuses missing pre-fix files, the companion test `test_a_fix_landed_elsewhere_is_verified_against_its_landing_commit` fails because it requires OK and `prefix_outcome == "failed"` for the same missing-file situation.

chunk_findings.detail: The `--landed` preflight still has the confirmed defect: the diff adds `_is_node_id`, but does not change the guard from `not any(...)` to `not all(...)`. Given a mixed `--regression-test` list such as `tests/test_x.py::test_a,tests/test_x.py`, the non-node entry `tests/test_x.py` cannot be checked, but `any` is true because one entry is a node id, so the guard lets the unverifiable entry through. The triage said this probe was confirmed; no `all(...)` substitution appears in this diff.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:bug_fixed

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_node_id("tests/test_x.py::")` returns `True` because the implementation only checks that `"::"` is present and the part before the first `"::"` ends in `.py`; it never requires a non-empty pytest node name after the separator. That string is not a valid pytest node id, so a `--regression-test` list containing only `tests/test_x.py::` passes the preflight instead of being refused as uncheckable, defeating the same guard the change is meant to enforce. The helper should also require the part after the first `"::"` to be non-empty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:_is_node_id

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--landed` branch returns `_regression_status(status, ev, G)` unconditionally. For a successful close such as `ddflow bug fixed B256be593f0 --landed <commit> --regression-test tests/test_x.py::test_bug` where the test fails on `landing[1]` and passes on `landing[0]`, `G.verify_regression_test` returns `status == "verified"`, but the code still returns immediately. That exits `bug_fixed` before the function’s normal completion path that records the bug closure and calls `_end_fix_task_landed`/`_drop_fix_task`; the command then prints “bug … closed” and returns OK even though the bug record is not closed and the fix task is not ended. The branch should only early-return for non-verified statuses, like the neighboring landed-before/after path for a verified regression.
